summary_en: This Phase 2 study tests quisinostat, a capsule drug, in adults with high-risk uveal melanoma after their primary tumor has been treated. Participants take 12 mg by mouth three times per week in 21-day cycles, for up to 17 cycles (up to 51 weeks), and are followed for up to 2 years after treatment ends. The main outcome measure is not stated; the stated purpose is to see whether quisinostat prevents the tumor from spreading.
summary_es: Este estudio de fase 2 evalúa quisinostat, un medicamento en cápsulas, en adultos con melanoma uveal de alto riesgo después de que se trató el tumor primario. Los participantes toman 12 mg por vía oral tres veces por semana en ciclos de 21 días, por hasta 17 ciclos (hasta 51 semanas), y se les da seguimiento hasta 2 años después de terminar el tratamiento. El resultado principal no está indicado; el propósito indicado es ver si quisinostat evita que el tumor se propague.
who_for: Uveal melanoma with a tumor at least 12 mm wide, with primary treatment finished within 183 days of starting study drug.
High-risk (class 2) result on a gene expression profiling test.
Age over 18, ECOG performance status 0 to 1, and life expectancy over 3 months.
Able to swallow and keep down oral medicine, and agree to use birth control.
not_for: Another cancer that is progressing or needs active treatment, with listed exceptions.
Prior adjuvant treatment for uveal melanoma after primary tumor therapy.
Prior use of histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitors.
Known HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C infection, with listed exceptions; HIV patients on combination antiretroviral therapy are excluded.
QTcB of 480 msec or higher, or a history of long QT syndrome.
